Dentists who provide snoring and sleep apnea solutions 
 
 
 
 
June 2, 2026 
 
The Honorable Mehmet Oz, MD, MBA 
Administrator 
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
U.S. Department of Health and Human Services  
7500 Security Boulevard 
Baltimore, MD 21244 
 
RE: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Patient Protection and Affordable 
Care Act; Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs 
for Medicare Advantage Organizations, Medicaid Managed Care Plans, 
State Medicaid Agencies, Childrenâ€™s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) 
Agencies and CHIP Managed Care Entities, and Issuers of Qualified 
Health Plans on the Federally-Facilitated Exchanges [CMS-0062-P] 
 
Dear Administrator Oz: 
 
On behalf of the American Academy of Dental Sleep Medicine (AADSM), thank 
you for the opportunity to submit comments in response to the proposed rule 
on Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs referenced 
above.  The AADSM is a national professional organization for dentists focused 
on the treatment of OSA and snoring. Our mission is to reduce the number of 
people with undiagnosed and untreated OSA, snoring, and related conditions, 
particularly through the use of oral appliances. To advance this mission, we 
offer education, professional development, and resources to dentists while 
promoting research, advocacy, and public awareness. We also develop and 
maintain evidence-based practice standards to ensure that oral appliance 
therapy is safely and effectively provided to patients.   
 
Given that oral appliances are generally characterized as durable medical 
equipment (DME) furnished under medical benefits, our comments are focused 
on the Request for Information (RFI) on Laboratory Services and Durable 
Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics, and Supplies (DMEPOS) items.  In 
this RFI, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) seeks 
information on prior authorization requirements for DMEPOS items, including 
their impact on patient care and health care provider burden, opportunities to 
improve prior authorization processes, other issues that technology is not 
addressing, and more.  
 
AADSM appreciates CMSâ€™ interest in and attention to the matter of reducing 
burden associated with prior authorization processes for DMEPOS items.  As 
CMS is aware, prior authorization requirements and processes can delay 
medical care or even prevent patients from receiving care altogether. Delays in 
care are not in the best interest of patients and could contribute to additional 
medical issues that necessitate further treatment. For patients with sleep 
apnea, delays in treatment can be potentially life-threatening.  Sleep apnea is 
associated with increased motor vehicle accidents and serious health problems,  
 
 
 
including high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, stroke, diabetes, impaired cognitive function, 
and depression, as well as poor quality of life.  Effective, timely treatment to manage sleep apnea is 
critical in helping improve the overall health and well-being of patients, and oral appliances are an 
important treatment option that patients should be able to readily access. 
 
For providers, prior authorization requirements require staff time and increase paperwork, contributing 
to higher practice expenses. Furthermore, challenges dealing with insurance companies can contribute 
to frustration and burnout for health professionals. In some cases, our members report that processing 
prior authorization requests may take more time than actually providing the service. 
 
Given the challenges that prior authorization presents, AADSM would support ways to reduce prior 
authorization requirements, or at minimum streamline prior authorization processes across payer types, 
including through the use of technology to evaluate medical necessity and to assess for applicability of 
â€œsame or similarâ€ restrictions or â€œduplicate equipmentâ€ edits. To the extent that prior authorization is 
applied to oral appliances, provision of instantaneous/real-time approval should be maximized to 
reduce lag time from referral to delivery. Additionally, we highlight the need to improve efficiency of 
payer portals for submitting prior authorization requests; in many cases, supporting documentation 
cannot be submitted with an initial request, thereby leading to denials and lengthy appeals processes.   
 
We also call attention to considerations specific prior authorization requests for DME furnished by out-
of-network providers.  In our membersâ€™ experience, prior authorization approvals are not accompanied 
by any information regarding the reimbursement rate for the oral appliance.  As a result, providers are 
unable to provide details on patientsâ€™ financial responsibility, which can affect whether patients accept 
treatment.  Technology could readily be leveraged to include information on reimbursement rates along 
with prior authorization approval notices, such that patients can have full information when making 
treatment decisions.  
 
Thank you for your consideration of our comments. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to 
reach out to me at pjacobs@aadsm.org with any questions. 
 
Sincerely, 
 
Paul Jacobs, DDS, Diplomate, ABDSM 
AADSM President
analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** American Academy of Dental Sleep Medicine (AADSM); signed by Paul Jacobs, DDS, Diplomate, ABDSM, AADSM President.
- **Stakeholder type:** Professional Association
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** National professional organization for dentists treating obstructive sleep apnea and snoring; develops evidence-based practice standards for oral appliance therapy.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

AADSM responds to the DMEPOS RFI because oral appliances for sleep apnea are generally DME under medical benefits. It supports reducing or streamlining DMEPOS prior authorization, maximizing real-time approvals for oral appliances, improving payer portals so supporting documentation can be submitted initially, using technology to evaluate medical necessity and same/similar or duplicate-equipment edits, and including reimbursement-rate information with approvals for out-of-network providers.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** GENERAL/RFI; API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING/API-USAGE-METRICS by analogy to portal and transparency improvements.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** CMS-0062-P.
- **Standards referenced:** Technology-enabled PA; payer portals; no specific FHIR IGs or NCPDP standards.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: DMEPOS PA burden for oral appliances**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Prior authorization can delay or prevent sleep apnea treatment and add provider paperwork and staff time.
- **Specific request:** Reduce PA requirements or streamline processes across payer types.

**Topic 2: Real-time approvals**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Delays between referral and delivery can be harmful for sleep apnea patients.
- **Specific request:** Maximize instantaneous or real-time approval for oral appliances when PA applies.

**Topic 3: Technology for medical necessity and edits**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support/Modify
- **Rationale:** Technology can assess medical necessity and same/similar or duplicate equipment restrictions more efficiently.
- **Specific request:** Use technology to streamline DMEPOS PA adjudication and reduce lag time.

**Topic 4: Payer portal documentation**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Payer portals sometimes prevent supporting documentation from being submitted with the initial request, causing denials and appeals.
- **Specific request:** Improve portal efficiency to accept complete supporting documentation at initial submission.

**Topic 5: Reimbursement transparency for out-of-network providers**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** PA approvals without reimbursement rates prevent providers from estimating patient financial responsibility.
- **Specific request:** Include reimbursement-rate information with PA approval notices for out-of-network DME providers.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S66-S82:** AADSM directly responds to the DMEPOS RFI, addressing patient care impact, provider burden, technology opportunities, portal issues, and reimbursement transparency.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Reduce DMEPOS PA requirements where possible.
2. Streamline PA processes across payer types.
3. Maximize real-time approval for oral appliance therapy.
4. Use technology to evaluate medical necessity and same/similar or duplicate-equipment edits.
5. Improve payer portals to allow supporting documentation at initial submission.
6. Include reimbursement-rate information with out-of-network PA approvals.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** Treatment delays, provider paperwork, staff time, payer portal inefficiency, denials from incomplete initial submissions, appeals delays, and lack of reimbursement transparency.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Untreated sleep apnea risks including motor vehicle accidents, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, stroke, diabetes, impaired cognitive function, depression, poor quality of life, provider burnout, and patient uncertainty about financial responsibility.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Inefficient payer portals, inability to submit supporting documentation with initial PA requests, lack of reimbursement data on approvals, and payer variation.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** None quantified.
- **Studies or research referenced:** None.
- **Examples provided:** Oral appliances for obstructive sleep apnea; same/similar restrictions; duplicate equipment edits; out-of-network provider reimbursement rates.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Sleep apnea patients, dentists furnishing oral appliances, out-of-network DME providers, payer portal users, and health plans.
- **Economic implications:** PA creates higher practice expenses; lack of reimbursement information affects patient treatment decisions.
- **Technical feasibility:** AADSM believes technology can support real-time approvals, medical necessity assessment, and reimbursement transparency.
- **Patient care impact:** Delays in oral appliance therapy may worsen serious sleep apnea-related health risks.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Supportive of burden reduction; requests DMEPOS-specific modifications
- **Tone:** Professional, clinical, operational
- **Priority level:** Medium

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "For patients with sleep apnea, delays in treatment can be potentially life-threatening." - Context: Patient risk from PA delays.
2. "Processing prior authorization requests may take more time than actually providing the service." - Context: Provider burden.
3. "Provision of instantaneous/real-time approval should be maximized." - Context: Recommendation for oral appliances.
4. "Technology could readily be leveraged to include information on reimbursement rates." - Context: Out-of-network transparency recommendation.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - Staff time, paperwork, practice expense, and burnout are central concerns.
- [x] **COST-RESOURCES** - Discusses practice expenses and patient financial responsibility.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - Supports technology for real-time approvals, edits, and reimbursement data.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - Focuses on timely access to sleep apnea oral appliances.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** - Requests reimbursement-rate information and better portal documentation.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - Critiques payer portals and current PA documentation workflows.
